Plan:
1. Reproduce `argparse` for `--a` with matching help/error text and exit codes, including `-h`, `--help`, `--a=value`, missing value, and unknown arguments.
2. Implement a local YAML pipeline under `/output/lib` with separate scan/parse/construct/dump modules so the entry file only wires CLI to serializer behavior.
3. Validate the Node output against the bundled executable on representative scalars, tagged values, sequences, mappings, and failure cases, then adjust formatting until byte-level output matches.

I have enough CLI shape to start coding, but PyYAML’s string-style decisions are the main fidelity risk. I’m sampling those now so the dumper can preserve ambiguous scalars the same way instead of overquoting or changing types.

I’m evaluating whether a vendored local YAML engine will save time without sacrificing fidelity. The parser side is the hard part; if the emitter shape is close enough to PyYAML, I can wrap it locally and keep the runtime dependency-free.

item.text: PyYAML uses indentless block sequences when a mapping value is a non-empty sequence. My emitter was nesting those by two spaces, so I’m switching that branch to the same indentation level as the key.
